title: semantic-index-swap-safety-and-compatibility-matrix
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Create a robust migration path and compatibility matrix to safely onboard new vector models and swap indexes used by the embeddings+reranker pipeline. The goal is to avoid semantic regressions, control latency regressions, and provide per-tenant rollback and fallback behavior during model swaps.
background: Recent model swaps in staging produced subtle score shifts causing QA failures in reranking tests and a 12% drop in recall on a tenant's search flows. Current rollout primitives allow traffic splits but lack semantic compatibility checks, automated reindex signaling, and an agreed on set of regression thresholds to gate rollout progress.
proposed_solution: Design and publish a compatibility matrix that maps old model family fingerprints to candidate new models with expected vector space shifts and normalization guidance.

Implement an automated regression harness that runs synthetic prompt/queries (canon set + tenant-specific seed sets) to compute stability signals: cosine shift distribution, top-k overlap, reranker delta, and recall@k change.

Extend the embeddings gateway to support a 'compatibility mode' that can return both old and new vectors for a sample subset (side-by-side) and compute a lightweight delta metric in-line for telemetry.
Provide a migration operator that can mark indexes for incremental re-embedding and surface progress in Console; support tenant-scoped windowed reindexing to bound compute and IO costs.
Add a policy engine for rollouts: canary size, quality thresholds (eg. median cosine shift < 0.04 and recall@10 drop < 2%), step-up rules, automatic pause/fail and rollback hooks.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal bench canary — run compatibility harness on curated corpora (3 days).
Stage 1: Staging tenants (5–10 low-risk customers) — enable dual-vectors and collect telemetry for 7 days.
Stage 2: Controlled production canary — 1% traffic with automated gating and daily manual review.
Stage 3: Progressive ramp — auto-increase by 3x/day while meeting gates; provide tenant opt-out feature.
Stage 4: Full flip with reindex window scheduling and post-swap observational period (14 days).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published in Console and docs with at least three example model family mappings.
Automated regression harness implemented and runs as part of onboarding jobs producing daily reports.
Gateway supports dual-vector sampling mode and emits per-request delta metrics to telemetry pipeline.
Rollout policy implemented with automated pause/rollback iff quality gates are breached.
At least two internal test tenants completed full swap with no customer-visible regressions and metrics captured in dashboards.
technical_notes: Cosine shift calibrated per-dataset: use robust estimators (median absolute deviation) rather than mean because tail outliers from long documents bias averages.
Normalize vectors using the same preprocessing pipeline as the old model (tokenization, truncation heuristics) to reduce surface differences.
Store vector provenance metadata (model_id, version, normalization_hash) in index to allow mixed-version queries and targeted TTL reembed.
Reindex operator should support chunked snapshots and resumable jobs to tolerate infra interruptions.
For latency-sensitive tenants, support 'sticky fallback' routing that pins requests to old model variants when a tenant is within a degraded interval.
testing_plan: Unit tests for compatibility matrix generator and threshold checks.
Integration test that exercises dual-vector path and verifies telemetry emission to the ingestion pipeline.
Synthetic regression suite: 12k queries across general, conversational, and domain-specific sets; evaluate top-1/3/10 overlap and reranker delta.
Load test with mixed-version query traffic to validate latency SLOs and batching behavior under dual-vector sampling.
Chaos test to simulate reindex operator failures and validate resumability and rollback triggers.
observations_and_risks: Risk: New models may systematically shift similarity structure for some corpora (eg. dense vs. sparse alignment) requiring per-tenant tuning.
Risk: Reindexing large tenant corpora could be costly; need quota and backpressure controls to avoid cluster thrash.
Risk: Telemetry signal noise during low-traffic tenants may produce false positives; plan to require minimum sample sizes before gating decisions.
Observation: Early side-by-side vector sampling produced stable top-5 overlap for general models but showed variance for domain-specialized corpora.
